articles.title: Do we really need clothes delivered in under an hour? Target’s Uber Eats deal is convenience culture gone wild | Maggie Zhou
articles.summary: The time lag between ordering a meal and its packaging hitting your rubbish bin is ridiculously brief. Will items bought through this partnership be treated differently?
body: I n a move nobody outside of boardrooms asked for, Target has become the first fashion retailer in Australia to make its products available to order via the Uber Eats app as of September. This means that a “curated” selection of 25,000 of Target’s products can arrive at your door in under an hour, thanks to Uber Eats’ “on-demand” delivery.

It follows Bunnings’ introduction to the platform in February, and Kmart appears to be following suit with Uber delivery available on some eligible orders. Big W has also joined in on the action, with more than 35,000 Big W “essentials” (their words, not mine) now ready to be delivered to your home in 60 minutes via DoorDash.

You can buy women’s heels, fashion jewellery, pyjamas and men’s suits, jocks and Christmas merch. You can buy homewares, baby goods, accessories, toys and beauty products, too. This sits side-by-side with Uber Eats’ main offerings of, well, things you can eat.
points: The time lag between ordering a meal and its packaging hitting your rubbish bin is ridiculously brief.
Will items bought through this partnership be treated differently?

articles.title: A job that changed me: On midnight shifts as a Subway ‘sandwich artist’, I served clubbers, cops and sailors
articles.summary: In Perth’s nightlife precinct in the 1990s, I made a lot of sandwiches – but the sandwiches also made me. Delivering pizzas, with all due respect, was a cruisy gig that fit in with my uni commitments.
body: The job’s biggest downside was that it didn’t pay much, especially once you factored in the costs of fuel and vehicle maintenance. So I applied for a job as a “sandwich artist” at Subway in Northbridge, Perth’s nightlife district. I figured that switching to a job where I was on my feet instead of on the road would significantly extend the life expectancy of my hand-me-down Mitsubishi Magna.

Working at Subway was more demanding than navigating apartment block intercoms and trying not to forget people’s garlic bread. Bins needed to be emptied. Bread was baked daily. Tables were continually sprayed and wiped. Salads and fillings required washing, slicing and cooking. Kind of. For one particular sandwich filling, I squeezed biblical amounts of mayo on to shredded seafood extender and massaged the lot by hand.
None of this was roquette science but that didn’t stop me from finding pride in being a tiny, hard-working cog in the restaurant machine.
I spent almost two years working from midnight till 5am every Saturday and experienced the full spectrum of late-night characters out and about in Perth.

articles.title: Where Chef Eric Sze Eats on His Day Off in NYC
articles.summary: Chef Eric Sze, the owner of NYC’s Wenwen, shows us the bakeries, pizzerias, and restaurants he visits weekly for everything from simple baguette sandwiches to oversized wontons.
body: Sze starts his day off with a sandwich at Bakeri; his go-to order is honey, apple, and brie layered on a crunchy baguette. Then he heads to The Meat Hook, Wenwen’s meat supplier, to get a specialty cut of steak and dry-aged short ribs for dinner. Next, he grabs a whole, crispy, NY-style pie at Chrissy’s Pizza (chef Chris Hansell has been perfecting this pie for years). The jalapeño and garlic pie has perfect proportions of each ingredient, all on a doughy, yeasted crust.

For his final stop, Sze goes to Maxi’s Noodle 2 in Flushing for the nostalgic Chinese food he’s craved since leaving Taiwan. Owner Maxi Lau-O’Keefe teaches him how to make her iconic wontons, filled with shrimp and pork before being expertly folded. After being humbled by the complex folding process, Sze settles in for a soup full of thin noodles made with duck eggs and those classic wontons, alongside beef soup.
Watch the most recent episode of Chef’s Day Off to see how chef Eric Sze spends his day off at his favorite restaurants, bakeries, and butcher shops around New York City.

articles.title: Do Female Writers Have to Turn Themselves Into a Brand While Men Get a Pass?
articles.summary: I’ve never heard a male writer agonize over the tension between writing and being a public figure. It’s the women who are starting Substacks and attending to social media.
body: I came home to a football-size bubble on the kitchen ceiling. It jiggled when I touched it, swollen with water from a leak I couldn’t see. I was still trying to decide what to do when my phone vibrated with an email. A single sentence from a stranger: Men abuse women because of women like you.

Earlier that week, I’d published a piece about leaving a toxic relationship for a job in Death Valley National Park. It was very personal, even for a personal essay. The initial response was a flood of kindness, which I naively thought would last. It didn’t. The email led me to the comments, the messages on Instagram, Facebook. The bubble on the ceiling expanded, the pressure building.
I called family members, friends. Well, it does come with the territory, one of them said.

The circumstances vary, but this experience is one shared by many writers. We dream of landing bylines and book deals, but few resources prepare us for the attention—and occasionally harassment—that comes with writing for a wide audience. You are not a celebrity, but you still occupy a space where hundreds, thousands, even millions of people can judge you.

articles.title: I’m So Glad That Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan Have Each Other
articles.summary: Every straight woman needs a lesbian bestie to be so appalled at how straight men are moving in 2026 that she actually raises said straight friend’s standards.
body: Love is a many-splendored thing, especially when you’re gawking at it from the outside. In this new column, we’ll be examining the celebrity couples—or, occasionally, friend pairs—who give us hope for our own romantic futures as we try to learn what we can from their well-documented bonds.

It has historically been a taxing (if not outright toxic) thing to be a young, female pop star; remember the “Britney vs. Christina” dichotomy that outright pitted two of the most famous female performers in the country against each other in the early aughts? Yet the long-standing friendship between Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan flies in the face of all that.

To borrow a phrase from Rodrigo’s earlier work, it’s brutal out here—not only for young women attempting to date, but also women of any age in the public eye—and I, for one, am really glad that Rodrigo and Roan are leaning on each other to make art, eat donuts, and complain about being ghosted. Isn’t that the true meaning of friendship, no matter how famous you both are?

articles.title: I Tried Strava's New Strength Coach Feature, and I'm Optimistic
articles.summary: Strava has built its reputation on runs, rides, and swims. Strength training, however, has always felt like an afterthought in the app. Strava is trying to close that gap with its new guided strength workouts, and I spent some time with the beginner session to see whether it delivers.
body: The update brings guided workouts directly in the app. Instead of just logging that you lifted, you're walked through each exercise with animations, and you track sets and reps live as you go. Tap into any exercise, and you'll find form guidance, tips, and the specific muscles it targets.

When you finish, everything (every exercise, set, and rep) is saved automatically to your activity through the Workout Log. Your muscle map then updates to show where the effort went, which is a neat way to see at a glance whether you've been neglecting certain areas.

I started with the beginner workout, and I want to be clear about who it's for: true beginners. There's no equipment required, so you don't need dumbbells, bands, or a gym membership. If you've been lifting for years, this isn't going to challenge you—but that's clearly not the point. For this first workout, it's designed to lower the barrier to entry.

The interface is clean and easy to use. I especially liked the graphics, which make it simple to follow along without having to pause and decipher what a movement is supposed to look like. Everything worked smoothly throughout, with no glitches, lag, or lost progress.
points: Strava has built its reputation on runs, rides, and swims.

articles.title: Inside Ejae and Samuel Kim’s Garden Wedding at Her Grandfather’s Former Home in Seoul
articles.summary: The ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ star Ejae married on October 17 in Korea, with a wedding wardrobe that included custom Danielle Frankel and Zac Posen looks and a traditional Paebaek ceremony.
body: Musical artist Ejae and producer-turned-computer programmer Samuel Kim’s relationship first began as a creative collaboration. A mutual friend set the two up for a songwriting session at Sam’s home studio in May 2017. “We worked on a couple of songs, but mostly, we just connected,” Ejae recalls. “We both loved anime and the same kind of music.” The two kept things professional—until a night out to see Sam’s roommate’s band perform. “Later that night, [he] confessed his feelings,” the singer says. “We've been together ever since.”

articles.title: 11 Types of Vinegar: A Guide to Cooking With Them and More
articles.summary: From white to red to black, these are the vinegars to know and love.
body: There are an awful lot of vinegars in the world—which ones you cook with depends entirely on your favorite flavors and what you’re making. Maybe you favor red wine vinegar for the punchy tang it brings to salad dressing. Or you can’t imagine a bowl of white rice without the gentle acidity of seasoned rice vinegar running through it. Perhaps you fall asleep at night dreaming of bowls of vanilla ice cream covered in ripe summer strawberries dripping with balsamic vinegar.

Whether you’re the kind of cook who has a favorite vinegar for every occasion or simply grabs whichever bottle is closest to the stove, it pays to know what you’re working with. You can often substitute one vinegar for another, but it's worth being strategic. “Each vinegar contributes its own flavor and character rather than just adding acidity,” says Sathish Kumar, the head chef of Indienne in New York and Chicago.
So which bottles deserve a spot in your pantry? We’re breaking down 11 types of vinegar, what to use them for, and substitutions that work in a pinch.

articles.title: A Frequent Flier’s Guide to Every Single United Lounge at Newark Airport
articles.summary: From premium bars and wellness rooms to a full-service restaurant, here’s what to expect at each United Club and lounge at Newark.
body: All told, they hit that perfect mix of the comfort of your local coffee shop, the suaveness of boutique hotel design, and delectable fresh-made food options that fuel you instead of weighing you down. Each is conveniently open from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, with the exception of the location near Gate C123, which is open until 10:30 p.m.
The United Club near gate C123 features a full-service coffee bar, premium bar, wellness room, and spa-like shower suites.

United first started its transformation of its Newark lounges when it opened the doors to this 30,000 square-foot space with 480 seats in May 2022. And with it, it made a statement. These were no longer just utilitarian lounges for a quick refresh and refuel before flights. These are design-forward spaces that meld that pre-flight care and comfort with boutique hotel-style decor rooted in its New York City and New Jersey culture.
